OpenAI cash burn projections compute spending 2026 The Information

sources_considered.why: OpenAI CEO's statement on falling price per unit of AI. It is about prices, not costs.
Reuters/FT report showing OpenAI's total compute spending rising sharply.
Secondary summary. The Reuters/FT report is closer to the source.

receipt.public_excerpt: OpenAI held its annual DevDay developer conference on Tuesday, where the artificial intelligence company announced a flurry of new products and features.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI was operating after the two-year mark, so the survival condition is met.

receipt.public_excerpt: The cost to use a given level of AI falls about 10x every 12 months, and lower prices lead to much more use.

evidence_items.explanation: On a per-unit, fixed-capability reading, prices fell by well over ten times. But this is a statement about prices, much of the 150x drop came before the post, and it describes steady declines, not one breakthrough.

metric_scope.metric: price per token at a given capability level

evidence_items.publisher: Reuters (via The Star), citing Financial Times

receipt.public_excerpt: OpenAI forecasts spending about $856 billion on computing power and infrastructure by the end of 2030, its largest expense category

evidence_items.explanation: On a total-spending reading, the costs of building and running OpenAI's models went up, not down. This is a forecast of spending, not a measure of unit cost.

unresolved_gaps: OpenAI has not published its own per-unit training or inference costs. Customer prices are not costs.
The speaker did not say whether he meant total costs or unit costs, and the two readings give opposite answers.
No source identifies one 'significant breakthrough' rather than steady gains.
